fields.expected: I want to work on AI systems that have a concrete user, a real failure mode, and something testable, and infrastructure mapping fits that closely. Most of my best work has come from the same pattern. At Summer Atlantic Capital I built the machine-learning core of an anomaly-detection system, including the event-ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI microservice, temporal sequence models over event streams, and a learning-to-rank layer for prioritizing alerts. The technical modeling was only half of it. An anomaly system that fires too often just replaces one problem with another, so I spent as much time on prioritization and on an RAG explanation layer that made outputs legible to human analysts. That is the part I would want to do at Cyvl: turn sensor and model output into something a person can actually act on. I also like that the role is full-stack. I built and shipped ClarityAtlas, an iOS health product, end to end with Swift, SwiftUI, and Supabase into a live Hopkins pilot with 30+ users, which is the same React/Python/Supabase kind of ownership this posting describes. My goal right now is to own substantial pieces of a real system on a small team, not isolated tickets, and being in-office five days a week in Boston is how I'd learn fastest.
